overview: AUKUS is a security partnership among Australia, the United Kingdom and the United States that includes helping Australia get nuclear-powered submarines and sharing advanced defense technology. Current law lets some defense goods and services be shared among the three countries without the usual individual export licenses, but excludes certain sensitive categories of items. This short bill amends the Arms Export Control Act to remove three of those excluded categories, so more types of defense items could be shared under the AUKUS licensing exemption. As of July 27, 2026, the Senate Foreign Relations Committee had approved it and it was waiting for a vote by the full Senate.
for: Supporters say cutting export-license red tape between close allies speeds up joint defense work and makes the AUKUS partnership work as intended.
against: Critics say loosening controls on sensitive military technology increases the risk of it leaking to others, and that Congress gives up some case-by-case review of those transfers.
